newsitem.title: INDIA: 275 bodies recovered from air crash site - agency.
newsitem.headline: 275 bodies recovered from air crash site - agency.

text.p: Indian rescuers have recovered 275 bodies from the site where two airliners crashed on Tuesday in the world's worst mid-air collision, the United News of India (UNI) news agency reported.
"Late tonight, 275 bodies had been recovered from the debris and taken to Dadri and Bhiwani civil hospitals and some private hospitals," UNI reported.

About 350 people were feared dead after a Saudi Arabian Boeing 747 passenger plane and a Kazakh Ilyushin Il-76 cargo aircraft collided at between 14,000 and 15,000 feet. The Saudi plane had just taken off from New Delhi and the Ilyushin was descending.
Scores of bodies, some of them women and children, lay burning in fields amid the scattered remnants of the two aircraft, the Press Trust of India quoted witnesses as saying.
UNI said two major hospitals in New Delhi, the Indian capital about 80 km (50 miles) from the crash site, had been alerted to keep all facilities open for victims.
